content.comment_body: I have a [product_name] [article_no], and I'd like to know if it's compatible with [product_name] Access Tool. If it is, why does Excel 2019 give an error when I try to read a variable? The module connects, but in the formula cell I get a code incompatibility error '#VALUE#'. Can someone help me resolve this? For context, I am a beginner.

Please write your future posts in English, as it's the preferred language in this forum. In response to your question (translation): Yes, that [product_name] module is compatible with Excel 2019. Which version of [product_name] Access Tool are you using? Is it configured correctly?

My [product_name] Access Tool version is V2.1.0. I am using Windows 10 64-bit with Excel 2019. The network address and password are correct because it says it's connected to the module, but it returns a data format incompatibility error. In that case Excel shows the generic '#VALUE?' error.

Hello [user_name], Please try to ask your question in English, as this community uses a single language for clarity and better response rates. Here is the translation of your question: Regards, [user_name]
Take a screenshot of your Excel table showing your entries from the module variables.
I don't know what happened, but today, without changing anything, it's working.
Please use English for your posts.
I write in English, but when I publish the post, it appears in Italian. Why is this happening?

Hello [user_name], I'm glad your problem is resolved, thank you for your feedback. It seems you have auto-translate enabled in your browser, causing your posts to display in Italian. In Chrome, you can turn this feature off as follows: Regards, [user_name]

Despite no changes to the setup, the integration worked at a later time, suggesting the problem may be caused by unstable configuration, software, or environmental factors impacting the connection or data exchange.
